notes: Online-only loop: each configuration's "effect is measured with an A/B experiment whose result is written back to memory" (Sec 4). c1/c2: online sessions and watch time (Table 1); the next decision is driven by the A/B result. c3: na. c4: N, one A/B per round (R1-R3, Table 1); no repeats. c5: N, the second platform tests a different lever, not transfer of the selected gain. c6: N. c8: production, the A/B control is the live production configuration. c9: P, not na, because constraints are stated: "a numerical optimizer that keeps every change within a fixed operating budget" (Abstract), guardrails and human oversight (Sec 4). incident: none reported.

c1: ranking-ns, Recall@K/NDCG@K under "the leave-one-out protocol" (Sec 4.1); candidate set never stated. c2/c3: "All tuning decisions are made exclusively on the validation set ... Only the final configuration selected on the validation set is evaluated on the test set" (Sec 3.1). c4: P, "results are averaged over three independent runs" (Sec 4.1); no std or CI anywhere. c5: P, best validation N@10 (Table 2) and test results (Table 1) are reported separately, with a footnote that they are "not directly comparable" (Sec 4.6), so no explicit val-vs-test check; there is a cross-domain prior on unseen Baby (Fig 2). c6: Y, "The search budget is configured to favor the baselines: Grid Search enumerates all 729 configurations, and Bayesian Optimization runs for 500 trials" (Sec 4.1). VirtualMLE may also change some structural choices, so its space is somewhat larger. c8: tuned, the main comparison is "AutoML-tuned lightweight backbones" (Sec 4.1); generative baselines follow Zhou et al.'s setup. c9: Y, "The test set is completely hidden from the agent during exploration, and the data preparation pipeline is immutable" (Sec 3.1). incident: none reported.

Headline = System A, "1.82x Recall@6 lift ... over hand-tuned baselines" (Abstract). c1: full, "for each held-out book a customer purchased, the six nearest neighbors in embedding space are retrieved via a FAISS IVF+Flat index" over the catalog index (Sec II-A). c2/c3: test, the loop "keeps or discards based on a held-out scalar metric" (Sec I) and the reported peak is on that same "held-out evaluation set" (Sec V-A); no separate validation split. c4: P, the peak is "~2.6 sigma above the across-date mean" and "the across-date mean preserves a 1.63x lift" (Sec V-A), a noise estimate across evaluation dates without repeating a campaign. c5: P, across-date evaluation and full-scale re-testing of System B decisions (Sec V-A); the online pilot is not yet run. c6: N, config-level AutoResearch is still an LLM agent. c8: tuned, "The hand-tuned baseline was the product of four engineer-weeks of manual work" (Sec V-A). c9: P, "an immutable evaluator that the agent observes but cannot modify" (Sec II); test access not ruled out. incident: Y, System B: "introduce a guardrail ... to prevent the agent from gaming coherence at the expense of a meaningful hierarchy" (Sec III-D); metric fixation needed human QA.

c1: online, headline is "pushes GMV from -3.6% to +9.2% within 7 rounds" in production A/B (Sec 1, Table 4). c2: online, each round's parameters come from Optuna TPE on logged-data proxies, but which round is frozen and promoted is decided from online A/B ("decisions to freeze R7 parameters, conduct 7-day static A/B testing, and approve production rollout were all made by human operators based on snapshot-level A/B analysis", Sec 4.9). c3: na, no offline test split; offline proxies are search objectives only. c4: N, one A/B observation per round; no repeats or spread. c5: P, frozen R7 "validated through a 7-day A/B test (03-15 to 03-22)" before rollout (Sec 4.8.4), a later period; also a second market. c6: N, Optuna TPE is the inner engine of the system itself; no LLM-free ablation reported. c8: production, uplift vs the control group's current formula (Sec 4.2). c9: P, the LLM runs with "--sandbox read-only" (Sec 2.7); proposals go through schema validation and clamp ranges such as "Penalty weight clamp range [1,000, 80,000]" (App). incident: none reported.

Headline = "a matched comparison measured an offline improvement of 3.20 percentage points" in click hit-rate, plus +0.66% online (Abstract). c1: ranking-ns, offline replay "reconstructs a candidate pool and measures whether held-out engaged videos survive the top-K output" (Sec 4.2); the pool's size and construction are not stated. c2/c3: test, "Offline evaluation replays held-out pairs ... Its primary selection metric is click hit-rate at depth K" (Sec 4.4), and the reported 3.20 pp comes from the same offline evaluation; no separate validation split. c4: P, "The ±0.36 percentage-point band ... is an empirical tolerance from repeat publication. Two publications with the same model, configuration, and pinned data differed by 0.36 points" (Sec 5.1); no repeated campaign. c5: P, seven-day randomized online A/B of the selected model (Sec 5.5). c6: N. c8: production, the comparison base is the shared production baseline, with the interaction head as the only treatment (Sec 5.3). c9: P, isolated workers, read-only variant specs, date-order guards (Sec 4.4-4.6); no statement that evaluation data is unreachable. incident: Y, "a favorable result used an evaluation date inside the candidate model's training window, so the result was retracted" (Sec 4.7); also the pre-existing evaluation defect behind the -22 pp misattribution.

Headline = Tier-3 offline gains, e.g. "+2.557% relative improvement on the regression objective" on M* (Sec 6.6, Table 1). c1: auc, "offline metric suite like NE (Normalized Entropy) ... rMSE" (Sec 5). c2/c3: NS, candidates are triaged by significance "against the rolling baseline" (Sec 4.4); no split or evaluation window named. c4: P, "triggers an automatic re-run when within-run variance exceeds a threshold" (Sec 4.4), a rule to re-run noisy candidates; headline numbers have no spread. c5: N, no held-out or online check of the selected gain. c6: N, HPO/NAS appear only in related work. c8: production, the comparison is the rolling production baseline (Sec 4.4). c9: P, "edits ... in a sandboxed copy of the codebase" with "human-in-the-loop checkpoints at each stage boundary" (Sec 4.3, Abstract); test access not addressed. incident: none; "pretend to have completed tasks" (Sec 6.9) is a workflow failure, not metric inflation.

Headline coded = the closed loop the abstract marks "More importantly": "20 consecutive iterations over two weeks, improving offline Hitrate@200 by 23.6%" plus online A/B (Abstract, Sec 5). The alternative headline, single-proposal success rate S@1 = 0.6786, would be c1 other and c2 trainloss, since "S@k uses the actual loss decrease obtained from real execution" (Sec 4.1). c1: ranking-ns, Hitrate@200 of a recall model; candidate set not stated. c2/c3: NS, each direction is "trained, evaluated offline, and deployed online if successful" (Sec 5); the split and success criterion for the loop are not given. c4: N, single cumulative number. c5: P, online A/B July 1-5; "gains remained stable throughout the entire test window" (Sec 5). c6: N, baselines are human experts and general LLMs. c8: production, the loop evolves the production recall model; A/B against live control. c9: NS, no description of what the code agent can access. incident: none reported.

c1: online, headline is "a 4.829% improvement in GMV in a real-world short-video e-commerce recommendation system" (Abstract, Table 5). The offline evaluation scores strategy text for correctness and novelty (Table 2) and is not a rec metric. c2: online, the next round is chosen from "online A/B feedback" via the experiment tree (Sec 3.3). c3: na, no offline test split. c4: N, single lifts, no repeats. c5: N. c6: N, baselines are LLMs and RAG agents. c8: production, A/B against the production control; Table 3 also compares an expert strategy. c9: P, "parameter ranges, parameter types, and configuration consistency" checks plus agent and human review before launch (Sec 4). incident: none reported.

Headline = three-week Kuaishou deployment: "374 ideas into 10 launchable rollouts ... 3.7x business value over a manual engineer, a 0.561% user app-time gain" (Abstract). The model-side offline AUC study is secondary. c1/c2: online, "An Evaluation Agent conducts safe online rollout with guardrail-vetoed A/B judgment" (Abstract, Sec 6). c3: na. c4: N, headline numbers have no repeats. The "evidence from at least two independent runs" rule gates memory entries, not candidates (Sec 7). c5: N. c6: N. c8: production, comparisons are to the deployed production strategy and a manual engineer. c9: P, "Parameter changes must pass an engineering whitelist so that an agent cannot modify unauthorized scheduler or serving controls"; canary rollout (Sec 6). incident: none reported.

Operational outcomes only: "significantly reduces the human time required per experiment cycle and improves execution reliability" (Abstract); Sec 7 reports human bandwidth and major-fix steps over 31 iterations, with no model metric for selected ideas. c1: other (fix steps, zero-fix rate). c2: na, no selection result reported. c3: na, cannot apply without a selection result (the guide reserves na for online-only systems, so NS is the alternative). c4: N, single trajectory. c5: N. c6: N. c8: production, ideas are compared against "a common baseline with aligned training date ranges" of the industry model (Sec 5.2); NS would also be defensible. c9: P, "deterministic scripts enforce operational correctness" and per-idea state isolation (Abstract, Sec 3.1); no statement on evaluation-data access. incident: none reported.

Headline = "up to 5.54% offline improvement over the strongest baselines" plus online A/B (Abstract, Table 1). c1: ranking-ns, "We adopt leave-one-out evaluation and report Recall@5/10 ... NDCG@5/10" (Sec 3.1.1); candidate set not stated. c2/c3: NS, each round records "the offline evaluation metric vector" and a verdict (Eq. 2); no split named. c4: N, single numbers in Tables 1-3. c5: P, 7-day online A/B against production MGUI (Sec 3.5). c6: P, "auto-optimization (AutoML ...) applied to each base model" as Auto-MGUI/Auto-REG (Sec 3.1.2); search space and budget not stated. c8: untuned, "Training hyperparameters for both base models follow their original papers" (Sec 3.1.3). c9: NS, nothing on what the Engineer agent can reach. incident: none reported.

c1: sampled, headline "~20% relative improvement in NDCG" (Abstract). The offline proxy relies on in-batch negatives: "Because the Two-Tower model utilizes in-batch negative sampling, a smaller batch size ... providing fewer negative candidates per step" (Sec 5.2). Not stated for the final table, so ranking-ns is the alternative. c2/c3: NS, KEEP if "gamma(Phi_NS) > tau + epsilon" from the "evaluation suite" (Alg. 1); no split named. c4: N, single trajectory. c5: P, champion model deployed "in a production A/B test on live user traffic" (Sec 5.6, Table 2). c6: N. c8: production, "deployed directly on a production large-scale Two-Tower retrieval model"; relative to the production baseline. c9: P, pre-execution validation gate, "isolated branches" and VCS rollback (Fig 1, Alg. 1); test access not addressed. incident: Y, "drastically reducing the batch size (from 8k down to 1k) artificially inflated proxy metrics ... the system effectively 'hacked' the metric" (Sec 5.2).

Headline = best-bucket online lifts after five days, "up to +1.40% IPV ... improving over ROAM's best results" (Abstract, Table 7). c2: online, rounds are kept or changed from bucket A/B reads (Sec 3). c3: na, online-only. The design pre-registers a confirmation that "runs once" on "a freshly collected, held-out sample" (Sec 3.4), but no such result is reported; the headline is the best of 5 buckets on search data, so N is a possible reading. c4: N, the five buckets are different configurations, not repeats; ROAM vs PILOT "is before/after, not randomized" (Sec 6.3). c5: N, D_confirm is not reported. c6: N, ROAM is an LLM agent and the deterministic-only cell is "planned" but not run (Table 8). c8: production, lifts are vs the control bucket. c9: P, the Manager selects "only from a rule-generated legal-command envelope" and "deterministic services enforce all safety, statistical, and permission boundaries" (Abstract). incident: none; the paper lists cherry-picked dates or windows as out of bounds (Sec 3.3) and reports no case of the loop doing this.

Headline = "several successful production launches at YouTube", online metrics with CIs (Abstract, Table 1). c2: online. The Offline Agent ranks candidates by validation loss ("the resulting validation loss values are comparable", Sec 4.1), but the Online Agent decides which ones launch "against a hierarchy of north star business metrics" (Sec 4.2); val is the fast-loop answer. c3: na, the offline stage has only a validation proxy, no test split. c4: P, the agent ablation is "averaged over 6 independent runs" (Table 4); headline CIs come from A/B, not repeats. c5: P, offline-selected candidates go to online A/B (Table 1), a different population and metric. c6: N, HPO/NAS appear only in related work. c8: production, compared with launches in "the traditional, manual approach" on a production model (Sec 5.1). c9: P, fixed tools ("compute_loss", "compute_eval") and guardrails ("Keep Metric#3 <= +1%", prompt in Sec 4.2). The agent can run SQL over user logs (Sec 4.1), and nothing rules out access to evaluation data. incident: none reported.

Headline = one-month online A/B: "increases order volume by 0.71%, browsing depth by 0.34%, and clicked-category diversity by 0.48%" (Abstract). c2: online, candidates pass "bad-case retesting, traffic replay, human verification, and online A/B validation before deployment" (Sec 1); the final gate is online. c3: na, no offline test split; offline stages are bad-case retest and replay. c4: N, single lifts. c5: P, historical-traffic replay "measures generality and safety beyond the selected cases" (Sec 3.5), plus online rollout. c6: N. c8: production, "the control group retained the existing manually configured post-ranking strategies" (Sec 4.1). c9: P, "The LLM supplies only bounded parameters and cannot generate or modify the script" (Sec 3.5); typed, bounded actions. incident: none reported.

Headline = "0.94 nDCG@1" on a benchmark of 100 policy-selection instructions (Abstract): nDCG over the agent's choice of policies against labels, i.e. agent selection quality, not a rec metric, so other. c2: online, candidate policies come from online experiments and are promoted only if "95% confidence interval excludes zero for the primary metric" (statistical-significance guard, Sec 3.3). c3: na, policies are judged on online experiment data; no offline test. c4: N. c5: P, "Deployment across nine production surfaces demonstrates consistent metric improvements" (Abstract), with no detailed held-out comparison. c6: N, baselines are prompting and code-execution LLM methods. c8: production, policies are chosen relative to production controls in the source experiments; the main comparison is LLM baselines, which have no category in the guide. c9: P, "Specialized Agent Skills: modular, read-only resources" and deterministic feature-stability and significance hooks (Sec 3.2-3.3). incident: none reported.

Online loop: "each edited skill ... is executed by task agent ... and evaluates it through online A/B experiment. In parallel, a concurrent control group runs under the best configuration" (Sec 3.2). c1/c2: online, rewards are A/B short-term signals mapped by LRP to long-term reward; headline = advertising metric lifts vs baselines (Table 2). c3: na; the chronological train/val/test split is only for training the LRP predictor (Sec 5.1). c4: N. c5: N. c6: N, baselines are skill-optimization (LLM) and reward-model methods. c8: production, control runs the current best configuration. c9: P, the upper-level agent makes structured "atomic edits" (location, action, content) to skill documents executed by a frozen task agent, plus constraint-aware monitoring (Sec 3, Ethics). incident: none reported.
